verdict.delta_sentence: Compared with the nearer intent-classification reference, this board offers stronger tinted grouping but has more truncated labels, longer inter-region detours, and a looser frame balance that makes the flow less immediately readable.

sub_checks.name: frame_use
sub_checks.note: The ten regions occupy a broad grid, but the composition stops well above the bottom and left of the right edge, leaving a conspicuous empty lower and outer band.

sub_checks.name: corridors_and_air
sub_checks.note: Most nodes and chips have clear internal air, but several cross-region corridors carry long unlabeled runs, and labels such as “open p...” sit too close to adjacent shapes or lines.

sub_checks.name: grouping
sub_checks.note: Tinted, numbered regions clearly separate admission, caching, routing, capacity, scheduling, fallback, metering, and shadow evaluation, doing genuine grouping work.

sub_checks.name: color
sub_checks.note: Distinct section and flow hues are consistent and generally semantic, with red/orange signaling protection or retry paths and green supporting outcomes and accounting.

sub_checks.name: machinery_leakage
sub_checks.note: No crosshair waypoints are exposed, but the branch bar beneath eligible capacity and several arrowheads terminating at icon-like endpoints retain a mildly diagrammatic routing-machinery feel.

sub_checks.name: alignment_and_rhythm
sub_checks.note: The three-row regional grid establishes useful rhythm, but uneven column occupancy, the missing central/right regions, and numerous visibly truncated node labels weaken finish and registration.

sub_checks.name: edge_legibility
sub_checks.note: Local edges are mostly clean, but multiple blue, orange, red, and gray routes make long inter-region detours, run beside region borders, and create ambiguous visual proximity around the center-left corridors.

verdict.rank_order_sanity_note: The assigned scores and visual ordering agree: gc-decomp-harness ranks first at 7.5, intent-classification-2 second at 7.0, and the board under grade third at 6.5.
